But the question arises, How shall this be done?<div eID="gen17000" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17001" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">put ... among ... children--</hi>the Greek for adoption means, literally, "putting among the sons."<div eID="gen17001" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17002" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the children--</hi>that is, My children. "How shall I receive thee back into My family, after thou hast so long forsaken Me for idols?" The answer is, they would acknowledge Him as "Father," and no longer turn away from Him. God assumes the language of one wondering how so desperate apostates could be restored to His family and its privileges (compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.3">Eze 37:3</reference>; Calvin makes it, How the race of Abraham can be propagated again, being as it were dead); yet as His purpose has decreed it so, He shows how it shall be effected, namely, they shall receive from Him the spirit of adoption to cry, "My Father" (<reference osisRef="John.1.12">Joh 1:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.4.6">Ga 4:6</reference>). The elect are "children" already in God's purpose; this is the ground of the subsequent realization of this relationship (<reference osisRef="Eph.1.5">Ep 1:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.2.13">He 2:13</reference>).<div eID="gen17002" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17003" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">pleasant land--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Jer.11.5">Jr 11:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.6">Eze 20:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.11.16">Da 11:16</reference>, Margin).<div eID="gen17003" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17004" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heritage of ... hosts--</hi>a heritage the most goodly of all nations [Maurer]; or a "heritage possessed by powerful hosts" (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.38">De 4:38</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.2.9">Am 2:9</reference>). The rendering "splendors," instead of "hosts," is opposed by the fact that the Hebrew for "splendor" is not found in the plural. <div eID="gen17004" type="x-p"/>
entries.549722cbe06e2c77475165ff89a04a56e4f3e344: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9645"/><div sID="gen17005" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9645"/><hi type="bold">20. Surely--</hi>rather, "But."<div eID="gen17005" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17006" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">husband--</hi>literally, "friend." <div eID="gen17006" type="x-p"/>
entries.af109e8e833e34cb3ebf77d370479f9978471938: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9646"/><div sID="gen17007" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9646"/>21. In harmony with the preceding promises of God, the penitential confessions of Israel are heard.<div eID="gen17007" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17008" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">high places--</hi>The scene of their idolatries is the scene of their confessions. Compare <reference osisRef="Jer.3.23">Jr 3:23</reference>, in which they cast aside their trust in these idolatrous high places. The publicity of their penitence is also implied (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.7.29">Jr 7:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.48.38">48:38</reference>). <div eID="gen17008" type="x-p"/>
entries.39af9dd5f8656215570a9e55f975319cb4c65870: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9647"/><div sID="gen17009" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9647"/>22. Jehovah's renewed invitation (<reference osisRef="Jer.3.12">Jr 3:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.3.14">14</reference>) and their immediate response.<div eID="gen17009" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17010" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heal--</hi>forgive (<reference osisRef="2Chr.30.18">2Ch 30:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.30.20">20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.14.4">Ho 14:4</reference>).<div eID="gen17010" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17011" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto thee--</hi>rather, "in obedience to thee"; literally, "for thee" [Rosenmuller]. <div eID="gen17011" type="x-p"/>
entries.762d74a5edb84292273689f825245bb6e2227fa3: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9648"/><div sID="gen17012" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9648"/><hi type="bold">23. multitude of mountains--</hi>that is, the multitude of gods worshipped on them (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.121.1">Psa 121:1</reference>, 2, Margin). <div eID="gen17012" type="x-p"/>
entries.18a21f3af6097fe248ceccb7e684455c22e85878: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9649"/><div sID="gen17013" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9649"/><hi type="bold">24. shame--</hi>that is, the idols, whose worship only covers us with shame (<reference osisRef="Jer.11.13">Jr 11:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.9.10">Ho 9:10</reference>). So far from bringing us "salvation," they have cost us our cattle and even our children, whom we have sacrificed to them. <div eID="gen17013" type="x-p"/>
